title: Size writing time from a top answer
statement: Size the time for an extended written answer from how long a top-scoring answer takes to write, and protect that time when a lesson runs long.
example: One design sizes a top-scoring Grade 3 extended response at eleven or twelve sentences, about twelve to fifteen minutes of writing.
detail: A Grade 3 reading lesson design sizes a top-scoring extended response at eleven or twelve sentences, with an opening, connected ideas, evidence and a conclusion, and calls it twelve to fifteen minutes of writing for a secure child working from a plan (`g9/sources/Readventure - Lesson Design and Scaffolding - Updated.docx`, line 451). Shed to its protected spine, the ~900-word lesson with a full model leaves only 8:40 for the write, so it splits in two: one lesson runs through the modelling and ends on a plan, the next opens with a short recap and is almost entirely writing (lines 447-450 and 453). The written part is on the design's never-dropped list, as the only unaided evidence the lesson produces (lines 397-418).
